subject.title: [Bug]: Hundreds of repeated HTTP requests to 169.254.169.254:80 for the first 10 minutes after the startup

question: Should OpenClaw accept the linked Bedrock-local no-signal IMDS suppression now, or require additional live sandbox plus EC2/ECS/default-chain proof before merging it?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible and the candidate fix is focused, but the changed behavior sits on an auth-provider and metadata-service boundary where maintainers must choose the acceptable compatibility proof bar.

options.title: Require live credential-mode proof
options.body: Ask for or run exact-head proof for the no-signal sandbox path and at least one explicit Bedrock AWS default-chain path before merging the linked PR.

options.title: Accept source-backed proof
options.body: Merge the linked PR after normal review and CI if maintainers accept the dependency-source proof and contributor no-signal runtime output as sufficient for this boundary.

options.title: Choose a different auth policy
options.body: Keep the issue open and ask for a revised fix if maintainers want a different default-chain or IMDS opt-in model.

recommendation.title: Require live credential-mode proof
recommendation.body: Ask for or run exact-head proof for the no-signal sandbox path and at least one explicit Bedrock AWS default-chain path before merging the linked PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Most closely connected to the current provider-plugin memory adapter boundary and the prior merged Bedrock credential-gate fix.
